Title: Diagnosis of test `readOfLength0ShouldReturn0` failure in `BZip2CompressorInputStream.read(byte[], int, int)`

Details:
The test's failing part is the assertion checking that reading 0 bytes from the input stream should return 0. The test expects that calling `bzipIn.read(buffer, 1024, 0)` returns 0.

Reviewing the implementation of `BZip2CompressorInputStream.read(byte[], int, int)`:

- Lines 155-164 validate the input parameters `offs` and `len` for bounds correctness.
- Line 165 checks if the stream is closed.
- The main reading loop (line 172) attempts to fill the buffer from `offs` to `offs + len` by reading bytes from the underlying stream via `read0()`.
- The loop continues as long as `destOffs < hi` (i.e., there is space to read into) and `read0()` returns a non-negative byte.
- After the loop, line 177 sets `c` to -1 if no bytes were read (meaning `destOffs == offs`), else sets it to the number of bytes read.
- Finally, `c` is returned.

The problem is that if `len == 0`, the condition `destOffs < hi` at the start of the loop is false (since `hi = offs + 0 = offs`), so the loop never executes and no bytes are read.

Following this logic, `destOffs == offs` will be true, so `c` will be assigned to -1. This means that if length zero is requested for reading, the method returns -1 instead of 0.

According to the InputStream's contract in Java, when reading 0 bytes, the method `read(byte[], int, int)` should return 0 and not -1.

Hence, the bug is that `read` returns -1 instead of 0 when the requested length is 0.

The fix would be to add a special condition in the start of the method: if `len == 0`, return 0 immediately.

This explains the failure of the test assertion `Assert.assertEquals(0, bzipIn.read(buffer, 1024, 0));`.

Suggested method to fix:
- `org.apache.commons.compress.compressors.bzip2.BZip2CompressorInputStream.read(byte[], int, int)`

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
